newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen to inspect and standardise futures firms.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen to inspect and standardise futures firms.

text.p: Shenzhen authorities will launch an annual inspection of local futures brokerages on February 1 to help bring the futures market further into line, the Shenzhen Special Zone Daily said on Thursday.

The two-month investigation was part of a nationwide campaign by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, the country's top securities watchdog, to stamp out irregularities in China's fledgling futures market, the newspaper said.

The inspection would help Beijing and regional futures authorities upgrade management, the newspaper quoted Cao Ruming, head of Shenzhen Futures Management Office (SFMO), as saying at a meeting of local brokerage officials.
Brokerages which failed the inspection would be punished and could be shut down, Cao said.
He said the SFMO would withdraw the licences of firms that secretly conduct foreign exchange futures and illegal margin trading.
The SFMO would inspect 56 futures trading houses registered in Shenzhen and submit the results to CSRC in early May for examination, the newspaper said.
